name: Merchant Navy Deck Officer
title: Merchant Navy Deck Officer
intro: From Class 12 PCM to ship's Master: IMU CET, pre-sea training (B.Sc Nautical Science or DNS), deck-cadet sea time, then DG Shipping Second Mate, Chief Mate and Master certificates.
glance: B.Sc Nautical Science (3 yrs) or DNS (1 yr)

phases.title: Class 12 PCM
phases.summary: PCM average above 60% and English above 50%.
points: IMU asks for Class 12 Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics with a 60% PCM average for B.Sc Nautical Science.
At least 50% in English in Class 10 or 12.
Age limit, unmarried status, passport and DG Shipping medical/eyesight standards apply — check the current IMU notice.

phases.title: IMU CET
phases.summary: An online entrance; your rank decides institute and course.
points: IMU CET is the common entrance for nautical and marine engineering programmes at IMU and most DG Shipping-approved institutes.
DNS route: Class 12 PCM (60%), or a B.Sc in a listed science subject, or a B.E./B.Tech, as the IMU notification lists.
Many cadets join through a shipping-company sponsorship, which helps secure the onboard cadet berth.

phases.title: Pre-sea training
phases.summary: B.Sc Nautical Science (3 years) or DNS (1 year) at a DG Shipping-approved institute.
points: B.Sc Nautical Science is a 3-year degree; DNS is a 1-year diploma — both are deck-officer routes.
Only train at institutes listed as approved on the DG Shipping website; unapproved courses do not count.
Register for an INDoS number and get a Continuous Discharge Certificate (CDC) to sail.

phases.title: Deck Cadet and Second Mate
phases.summary: Onboard training with a record book, then the Second Mate Certificate of Competency.
points: Deck cadets train onboard with a training record book; the required sea time is set by DG Shipping and a stipend is paid.
Post-sea courses and DG Shipping written and oral exams lead to the Second Mate CoC.
Then you sail as Third/Second Officer; pay rises sharply once you hold a CoC.

phases.title: Chief Mate and Master
phases.summary: More sea time and exams lead to Chief Officer and Master.
points: Chief Mate and Master certificates each need their own sea time, post-sea courses and DG Shipping exams.
Growth path: Deck Cadet → 3rd Officer → 2nd Officer → Chief Officer → Master — it takes many years.
Ashore later: port operations, marine surveying, ship management, maritime training and DG Shipping roles.
